fields.Name: IT101 - Perplexity Decider Decision Model
fields.Description: Perplexity's pplx-decider-v1-27b decision model resolves from the synced metadata through AIDecisionRunner to the Decisions API request, with no network. PX1 Perplexity Decider v1 27B is an Active Decision model with PowerRank 59 whose effective Decision limits are 128 questions per call, 255 Choice options, 10 Score levels and 262,144 state tokens; it has one Perplexity Model Developer row, one Active Perplexity Inference Provider row naming the PerplexityDecision driver, the pplx-decider-v1-27b APIName and a 262,144-token input limit without streaming, and an active Realtime cost row at $0.04 per million input tokens with free output; the Perplexity vendor takes an API Key credential. PX2 ClassFactory.CreateInstance(BaseDecision, 'PerplexityDecision', key), with the class the package registered back on top for the call, returns the shipped PerplexityDecision class, whose endpoint is https://api.perplexity.ai/v1/decisions. PX3 a real AIDecisionRunner.ExecuteDecision on the Default Decision prompt, with override naming the Decider and the Perplexity vendor and a legacy apiKeys key, selects it with PerplexityDecision; the driver POSTs Perplexity's quickstart request verbatim (a noul, a choice and a score question about a review object) to https://api.perplexity.ai/v1/decisions with the key as the bearer; the quickstart's response, verbatim, comes back mapped (Score probabilities read by level index and keyed by level name); and the MJ: AI Prompt Runs row is recorded against the Decider and the Perplexity vendor, successful, with 367 input tokens and a cost priced from the model's cost row. PX4 a real API Key credential created through CredentialEngine (stored encrypted) and bound to the Decider's Perplexity model-vendor row sends its token as the bearer, not the credential's JSON. PX5 Default Decision's candidates are Jev on OpenRouter, then LLM Decision, then the power-matched fallbacks, the Decider among them; the runner selects the first of Jev and LLM Decision it has a credential for; with a Perplexity credential bound to the Decider's row the candidates and their order are the same, the Decider has a credential and is still behind both, and the selection does not change (the decision drivers are the shared scripted stand-in for these legs); and with every other decision driver replaced by one that fails with a ServiceUnavailable error, the run logs a failed attempt for each credentialed candidate ahead of the Decider, LLM Decision among them, and the Decider answers through PerplexityDecision with the bound token. PerplexityDecision is replaced for the whole bundle by a subclass that overrides only SendRequest, answers with the quickstart response only while a check arms it and refuses otherwise, so no check can reach api.perplexity.ai. Server transport by necessity: the stand-in is a ClassFactory registration in this process. Every prompt run, credential, binding and credential audit-log row the bundle creates is deleted, children first.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: Perplexity Decider v1 27B is usable as a Decision model: its metadata resolves with the right limits, driver, API name and price, the driver builds through the ClassFactory, and an AIDecisionRunner call naming it sends Perplexity's quickstart request, maps its response and records the run against the model and Perplexity; a bound credential sends its token, and Default Decision's selection is unchanged, the Decider being reached only by failover.
